_header: dusimagez shared test vectors v0.1.0 — THE contract every language binding must pass.
Rust, JS/WASM, Python, Go, PHP, Kotlin and Swift all run this file and must agree.
WHY SIZE BOUNDS, NOT OUTPUT HASHES:
Exact output bytes are encoder-dependent (libjpeg vs mozjpeg settings, PNG filter
choices, WebP/AVIF encoder versions). A byte hash would fail on a correct build that
merely encodes slightly differently. So cases assert what the contract actually
guarantees: output format, output dimensions, an upper bound on output size
(max_output_bytes), a lower bound on savings where the saving is structural
(min_saved_percent), report fields (quality_used, resized) and stable error codes.
A bound that is too tight is a false failure; bounds here are set from sizes
measured with the real CLI (`dusimagez mock` fixtures + `dusimagez compress`)
with headroom for reasonable encoder variation, so any gross failure (no
compression, wrong format, upscale, crash) fails.
FIXTURES — generated deterministically, never hand-made blobs:
Run `dusimagez mock` (CLI, crates/dusimagez-cli) with the `generate` command shown
on each fixture. Fixture names, kinds, sizes and formats ARE the contract;
if the mock flags change, update the `generate` strings but keep names/sizes.
Only two tiny PNGs are committed under shared/fixtures/ (6,484 bytes total):
shared/fixtures/solid-red-64x48.png    (solid red, 64x48)
shared/fixtures/gradient-64x48.png     (R varies with x, G varies with y, B=128)
All other fixtures are generated at test time by `dusimagez mock` and are NOT
committed. `kind` is one of solid | gradient | noise (mock-generated), or one of
the pseudo-fixtures empty | garbage (no file: 0 bytes, or plain-text bytes — the
harness builds them inline) used only for error-path cases.
Mock colour conventions (fixed seed in the CLI, no --seed flag): solid = RGB
(255,0,0); gradient = R=x, G=y, B=128; noise = seeded RNG bytes.
CASE FIELDS:
id       — stable, unique; the harness reports failures by id.
op       — compress | compress_to_size | compress_with_report | get_info | bulk.
fixture  — name of one fixture in `fixtures` (single-input ops).
fixtures — list of fixture names (op bulk only; one result per input, same order).
options  — CompressOptions as JSON. Keys use the Rust field names (snake_case).
For op compress_to_size, options.target_bytes IS the target argument.
For op compress, options.target_bytes (if present) means the same
target-size search via the one-call path (SPEC §2).
expect   — assertions. max_output_bytes: output must be <= this many bytes.
min_saved_percent: 100 * (input-output)/input must be >= this.
quality_used / resized: exact report fields (compress_with_report
and compress ops that return a report; for plain compress the harness
checks them via compress_with_report with the same options).
error_code: the op must fail with exactly this stable code.
results (bulk only): one expect object per input, in order.
notes    — human-readable rationale for a bound that looks surprising.
OPTION KEYS (the only keys a case may use — the validator enforces this):
quality, format, progressive, lossless, effort, subsampling,
png_compression_level, palette, preset, target_bytes, max_width, max_height,
strip_metadata, auto_orient, dpi, max_pixels, max_dimension.
Enum spellings: format: jpeg|png|webp|avif|gif|bmp; subsampling: S444|S422|S420;
preset: Web|Social|Print|Archive; strip_metadata: All|KeepExif|KeepIcc|KeepAll.
dpi is [x, y]. Defaults are per SPEC.md §2 (quality 80, strip_metadata All,
auto_orient true, max_pixels 120000000, max_dimension 16000).

cases.notes: The report path: same compression as compress-default, plus the full before/after report. resized is false (no max_width/max_height, no target-size downscale).
Default options. A solid-colour PNG is already tiny (about 2.8 KB input), so no min_saved_percent is asserted — re-encoding an already-optimal PNG may save ~0%.
Noise is incompressible, so the saving here is structural: quality 90 input (~432 KB) to quality 50 (~183 KB) is ~57% saved. Bound 40% leaves encoder margin.
Quality search alone reaches 200,000 bytes (quality ~55 gives ~183 KB); no downscale should be needed, so dimensions stay 800x600.
100 bytes is below what even an 80x60 lowest-quality noise JPEG needs. The core must fail with TARGET_SIZE_UNREACHABLE, not return an oversized file.
Web preset quality is a core default (see shared/spec.md); the bound is 1.3x the ~45 KB quality-90 input so any reasonable Web quality (70-90) passes.

Palette quantise on a smooth gradient can make the file LARGER than the already-tiny RGB input (~1.1 KB in, ~4 KB palette out) — that is correct behaviour, not a failure. The bound only guards against gross blow-up.
Lossless WebP of a smooth gradient is tiny (~0.2 KB reference). Bound 5,000 leaves wide encoder margin.
Downscale-only, aspect preserved: 1200x800 -> 600x400. Never upscale: max_width larger than the input width must leave dimensions unchanged (see SPEC §2).
Quality 0 is outside 1-100. Same expectation for quality 101.
0-byte input must fail with EMPTY_INPUT, not INVALID_IMAGE.
Plain-text bytes are not an image. If the bytes were a valid image in an unsupported container, the code would be UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT instead.
Same target-size search as compress_to_size, reached through the target_bytes option on the one-call path. Quality ~65 reaches ~12 KB, so 15,000 is reachable without downscale.
Explicit output format overrides the input format. Solid red at JPEG quality 80 is ~8 KB.
One result per input, same order, partial failure reported per item: the batch must NOT abort on the empty input, and the two good items must still succeed.
